newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand sets dates for 1999 APEC meetings.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand sets dates for 1999 APEC meetings.

text.p: New Zealand will host the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings in mid-September 1999, Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Monday.
Announcing dates for the meetings, Bolger said APEC would focus on its goal of free and open trade and investment by 2010 for developed member economies and 2020 for developing member economies.

"During 1999 APEC will also want to focus on, and contribute to, the World Trade Organisation (WTO) process as it gears up for a further set of global trade negotiations commencing at the turn of the century," he said in a statement.
The annual APEC work programme leads to a ministerial meeting of the foreign affairs and trade ministers of the 18 member economies, followed by an informal meeting of the leaders of those economies.
The meetings will be held in Auckland in mid-September 1999, with the foreign affairs and trade ministers meeting from September 10 and 11, and the APEC leaders meeting on September 13.

APEC groups the United States, Canada, Mexico, Chile, China, Japan, Australia, Brunei, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand.
